title: Make every line carry a turn in meaning, value, or relationship.
dek: In Chapter 12 of Story, Robert McKee distinguishes the text on the page from the deeper design of action, intention, and changing value. The practical discipline is to make each line do work inside the larger movement of the story.

meta.canon: Robert McKee, Story: Substance, Structure, Style, and the Principles of Screenwriting

marginNote.label: Apprenticeship Note
marginNote.body: A sentence is not alive because it sounds polished. Ask what changes when it is spoken: information, power, desire, risk, or the relationship between the people in the scene.

canon.heading: Give every line a job inside the turn.
canon.standfirst: Read Chapter 12, "The Text," from Robert McKee's Story on PDF pages 282-293 of the local edition. McKee asks the writer to treat language as the visible surface of deeper choices about action, character, and value.
canon.readerIntro: Read this chapter as a test of textual function. Mark lines that reveal information, conceal intention, shift power, change a value, or alter a relationship. Then ask whether the same meaning could be delivered more forcefully through behavior, subtext, or a sharper turn in the exchange.

blocks.label: 01 / The text is the visible surface of deeper design
paragraphs: McKee separates the words on the page from the story movement those words serve. Text matters because it gives form to choices, actions, and changes already organized beneath the surface.
The writer's task is therefore larger than making lines sound natural. A natural-sounding exchange can still be dramatically inert if nothing is risked, revealed, or changed.

blocks.label: 02 / Dialogue carries intention beneath the spoken words
paragraphs: Characters rarely state the whole of what they want. The pressure between the literal line and the underlying intention creates subtext, allowing the exchange to carry conflict without turning into explanation.
Listen for what each speaker is trying to obtain, avoid, or force. The line becomes useful when it advances that pursuit, even when its surface meaning appears simple.

blocks.label: 03 / Language becomes dramatic when value changes
paragraphs: A strong exchange does not merely pass information from one person to another. It moves the condition of the relationship or the scene from one value state toward another.

This gives revision a practical test: identify the value before the line, the pressure applied by the line, and the value after it. If nothing turns, the prose may be reporting rather than dramatizing.

blocks.label: 04 / The writer must make the surface answerable to the whole
paragraphs: A memorable phrase is not automatically a good line. Style earns its place when its rhythm, imagery, and precision intensify the action and reveal the particular mind speaking.
The text should feel inevitable in retrospect: concise enough to carry pressure, specific enough to belong to the character, and connected enough to the scene that removing it changes the movement.

passageAnchors: what is said and what is meant
closeReading: How does McKee distinguish the visible text from the deeper action and intention it carries?
Choose one exchange and write the literal objective of each speaker alongside the unstated objective beneath it.
Where does the chapter show language changing a value or relationship rather than merely delivering information?
What makes a line feel specific to a character instead of merely clever or polished?
Audit one page of dialogue: mark each line's function, the value before and after it, and the line you would cut first.

principle.heading: Make the sentence change the scene.
principle.body: Strong text is not decoration laid over structure. It is the precise surface through which intention, conflict, and changing value become audible to the reader or viewer.
principle.example: A founder does not tell a hesitant buyer, "You can trust us." She answers the buyer's specific objection, concedes the real risk, and names the next test. The words work because the relationship changes from guarded doubt to a conditional opening.
principle.practice: Take one conversation, landing-page section, or pitch. For every sentence, label the job it performs: reveal, conceal, pressure, reassure, turn, or invite. Rewrite the three sentences that perform no job so each one changes a value, intention, or relationship.

output.heading: Revise for movement, not polish.
output.body: Keep the lines that carry intention and change. Cut explanation that leaves the scene in the same condition, then sharpen the remaining language until it sounds inevitable for the person speaking.

signals.heading: Four current signals on making every message carry a concrete turn.

fieldNotes.title: TypeSafe AI bets on calibrated decisions instead of fluent output
fieldNotes.whatHappened: TypeSafe AI released Jev, a transformer-based model that produces probabilities or calibrated decisions rather than text. The company positions it as a cheaper, faster, and less hallucination-prone option for software automation because users define outputs in advance.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The product story gets sharper when the customer’s job is explicit. Instead of selling general intelligence, Jev frames the value around a bounded decision with a defined output and a clearer failure surface.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether developers prefer narrower, inspectable decision systems when reliability matters more than conversational breadth.

fieldNotes.title: Bonobos turns a fall campaign into episodic social storytelling
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Bonobos launched The Weekday Warrior Show, an episodic campaign starring Jack Quaid that runs across digital and social channels before leading audiences to the brand’s website and product content.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The campaign gives the brand position a repeated dramatic form instead of compressing the message into one polished claim. Each episode has to earn the next bit of attention while keeping the product promise in view.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether the episodic structure creates cumulative memory and site action, or merely produces isolated entertainment.

fieldNotes.title: Google moves product guidance into the YouTube shopping context
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Google announced a Business Agent beta for eligible YouTube ads, allowing viewers to ask product questions and receive tailored guidance without leaving the video context. It also made AI performance insights in Merchant Center broadly available across several markets.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: Discovery and action are being joined at the point where curiosity starts. The useful message is no longer only the ad line; it is the answer that changes a shopper from interest to a qualified next step.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether conversational guidance improves qualified action or simply adds another surface whose attribution is difficult to interpret.

fieldNotes.title: J.C. Penney launches a marketplace while tightening its value message
fieldNotes.whatHappened: J.C. Penney reported Q2 net sales down more than 8% year over year, while activewear, home, jewelry, beauty, and salon were relative bright spots. The retailer is launching a marketplace and continuing value-focused pricing and family-oriented holiday messaging.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The retailer is responding to pressure with several connected moves rather than one slogan: category proof, a new commerce route, and a clearer value frame. Each line of the turnaround has to change what the customer can do or believe.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether the marketplace and value promise reinforce one another or create another layer of choice without restoring preference.

tweets.title: A tiny trust turn in an everyday exchange
tweets.summary: A high-engagement fragment where a correction does not erase the effect of the original mistake: the relationship changes even after the speaker supplies better information.
tweets.text: Mistakenly gave some dude wrong directions then ran after him to correct myself when I figured it out. Only for him to say “don’t know if I can trust you now”
